notes: Two sites. 216 routes: a100-gpu-vm-002, 7 Nov 2026, Paddock 2eaedb5, Bench2Drive 7ec25d1 + patches 0001-0002 (record full220-836dda734659a86c-dda00e). Routes 3800, 11715, 23695 and 24071, set aside there for every model, driven later at b2d-fill-fastcode-shakaal (one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), Nov 2026, Paddock de22271 (PR #167 head), Bench2Drive 7ec25d1 + patches 0001-0003: patch 0003 removes a flow car 600 m from the hero before a large map puts it to sleep. Same settings as the 216: 5 Hz (planning_hz), waypoint_dt 0.5, early stop 30 s / 3 m + 4x Think2Drive's time, paddock's rig, onnxruntime's CUDA provider, no site env, up to three attempts a route. of the 220 routes pooled: 4 route(s) from 1 run(s) under `runs`, read from their results.json (sites recorded: none); 216 route(s) from tracked record bench2drive/meteor/full220-836dda734659a86c-dda00e, read from its upstream_scores.json (sha256 d5a5f1125cca; pooled at site a100-gpu-vm-002, its runs' sites recorded: none). A route scored under `runs` takes precedence over a record's row. duration_s, the evaluator's wall-clock seconds, is not in upstream_scores.json, so the 216 route(s) from tracked records carry none and metrics.json counts them missing, as for a route --resume reused. the declared_env of bench2drive/meteor/full220-836dda734659a86c-dda00e was written by scrub() before #175, which cut the directories after a template variable ({weights}/meteor/x.onnx became {weights}x.onnx, #173); it is exactly the runs' declared_env through that cut, so it counts as the same model.yaml env and the runs' value is recorded. 1 of 1 source runs kept no run.json, so their routes are attributed to meteor on the tree they were found in; config.model_env and the rest of config are what 1/1 source runs recorded. asked for a plan at 5 Hz, the planning_hz the model's model.yaml declared for these runs, the last plan followed in between. early stop (30 s without 3 m of route progress or 4x the expert's time on the route (none on the 9 route(s) here with no expert drive)): a car in a driving scene is expected to move, to finish in reasonable time and not to collide, so a route ended this way is a failed drive, scored as it stood when it ended (a collision's penalty included).
